feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital/public-sector communications leader: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target brand. It reads professionally, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with some structure and style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and technical breadth.  
- Good use of scale and impact signals: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, analytics stack, studio buildout.  
- Strong positioning for digital platform leadership through a mix of strategy, governance, CMS, analytics, multimedia, and AI/search work.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; consolidate to make the CV tighter and easier to scan.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond scope metrics—for example, improvements in engagement, efficiency, search performance, publishing speed, or campaign results.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists varies; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning).” No major misspellings found, but wording is occasionally repetitive (“supporting,” “strengthened,” “improve”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so it would benefit from sharper differentiation and a few concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrasing like “building the platforms” with more direct, outcome-oriented language: “Leads enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and editorial operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent roles to increase impact, e.g., “10,000+ page website,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten the list of capabilities to the most relevant 4–5 themes; “multimedia production” may be better left to skills/experience unless central to target roles.
- Consider a cleaner rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, governance, analytics, and editorial systems for mission-driven public-sector organizations. Delivers scalable content operations, AI-enabled search and user experiences, and cross-channel digital infrastructure supporting high-volume communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several phrases already covered in the subtitle and Core Competencies.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with recent projects; keep it brief here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and prioritize strategic/enterprise-level strengths over operational wording.
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Multi-channel digital communications leadership” for stronger seniority.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel digital communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows, swap “content experiences” for “content discovery” to sound more specific and less generic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid tool-specific terms already covered elsewhere.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the header and multiple role descriptions.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a short intro line such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise one-line achievement.
- Use parallel verb structure and tighten wording: e.g., “Created an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Where possible, add scale or result signals (audience, campaign use, adoption, event size, or business purpose) to increase impact.
- Standardize style: use “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and the advocacy video series substantially overlap with current NACo bullets; keep the footer more selective or more outcome-focused.
- “Built/Developed” repeats across all four items; vary verbs to avoid monotony.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting impact, platform modernization, and AI/search leadership.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, content operations, and campaign delivery for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcomes-oriented phrasing: “Designed/implemented” instead of “build and refine,” “led” instead of “advise,” “optimized” instead of “deliver technical troubleshooting.”
- Consolidate into 4 bullets, e.g.:
- Lead enterprise web and content operations improvements across Drupal, analytics, and cross-channel communications workflows.
- Designed modular campaign microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable toolkits to support member engagement.
- Implement CMS/front-end enhancements and resolve technical issues for large public-facing web properties.
- Lead AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and discovery UX.
- Add metrics if possible: number of sites/pages, users, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy gains, or engagement lifts.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” repeats themes from Director of Digital Media.
- Microsite and AI-search details overlap with Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level if those projects stay.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, overseeing web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget.”
- Prioritize the strongest achievements in 4–5 bullets: website migration, analytics stack, video studio, governance/operations, and channel reach only if you can add stronger metrics.
- Make outcomes more explicit: e.g., “Led redesign and migration of 10,000+ pages to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten phrasing: replace “along with”/“including” constructions with action + result; if possible add team size, budget size, email list size, engagement growth, production volume, or efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this higher-level or add distinct outcomes.
- Video/programming language overlaps with earlier NACo entries unless framed as building enterprise in-house studio capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around executional leadership, channel ownership, and concrete scale/results.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and ownership: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Combine overlapping workflow/editorial bullets into one stronger point: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”
- Make outcomes more specific where possible: add newsletter audience size, open/click performance, video cadence/views, or workflow gains (faster publishing, fewer bottlenecks, more cross-team alignment).
- Suggested version:
- Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, strengthening NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/ownership, not origin.
- “Governance/publishing standards/workflows” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating the same wording.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, differentiated language tied to leadership scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications leadership” to sound more current and concise.
- Change “Audience-focused content planning” to “Audience-centered content strategy” to elevate from tactical planning to strategic ownership.
- If space is tight, cut to 4 bullets by merging related ideas: “Editorial governance, workflows & content operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat almost verbatim from the header/Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one phrasing consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal & enterprise CMS platforms (Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: replace “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” with “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)” unless jQuery is specifically required for target roles
- Elevate impact-oriented skills: “CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, Airtable-based systems, AI-enabled search experiences”
- Possible rewrite: “Drupal & enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations • Workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave detailed tools like jQuery to the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies; keep it here only if it is a priority differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Make it more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit:
- Retitle to emphasize strategic value: **Analytics Infrastructure, Reporting & Optimization**
- Replace the list with grouped phrasing: **GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis**
- Consider adding one impact cue if used elsewhere in the CV style: **Built analytics infrastructure supporting enterprise web modernization and strategic decision-making**
- Keep “optimization” broad; avoid overly tactical terms unless you can support them with outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization**; keep Topline Skills higher-level and reserve tool detail for Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” may overlap with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; use one strategic phrase consistently.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and the Technical + IT “Multimedia & Creative Tools” section. It should emphasize operational leadership and delivery scope rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to higher-value capability statement, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- In-house studio and PTZ camera operations
- Multimedia workflows for advocacy, conferences and recurring programs
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to better match the studio-building achievement in recent roles.
- Replace “Hybrid and virtual event production” with “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” for tighter phrasing and stronger execution focus.
- If space allows, add scale/context instead of tools: “for advocacy programming, conferences and recurring content series.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “studio operations” are already implied by “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- PTZ camera systems may be too tool-specific here since Premiere Pro/Audition and other production tools already appear in Technical + IT.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize depth and recency or be trimmed.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider adding context: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites; multi-publisher governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; avoid “CMS” if this section is just platform names.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills item [2], which already lists the same platforms plus modernization and technical execution.
- GitHub Pages may feel lightweight versus the seniority of the profile unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, this section should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw coding languages to applied implementation: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless needed; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome-oriented qualifiers elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “used for CMS customization, campaign microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation.”
- Put the strongest/current tools first: JavaScript • API integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • Google Tag Manager • HTML/CSS • jQuery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM may fit better under Analytics/Optimization if you need to save space here.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since the CV already emphasizes automation and governance, this item should be tighter and grouped to highlight systems most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/issue management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first based on recent roles: Airtable, Power Automate, Jira, Asana; move older/general collaboration tools later.
- Consider trimming lower-value items if space is tight; Slack and Teams are expected workplace tools and add less differentiation than Airtable/Power Automate.
- If accurate, add a qualifier for impact: “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating that exact phrasing here without adding specificity.
- Airtable systems and workflow automation are also named under “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.”

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since recent roles emphasize enterprise email operations, this item should signal scale and purpose, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional context: **Higher Logic (member email/newsletters) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration/segmentation) • Mailchimp (campaign delivery)**
- If space allows, tie to impact in adjacent experience bullets instead of here: e.g., newsletter volume, audience size, segmentation, automation, or engagement improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating “email/social/video platforms” language here.
- “Engagement Systems” is broad; don’t imply CRM ownership unless you directly administered/build these systems.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics platforms already evidenced in the recent Director role. This item should be tightened to emphasize methods/capabilities, not just duplicate product names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Replace with a more capability-led line: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • KPI design • dashboard development • SEO analysis • experimentation/A/B testing**
- Keep the most credible, recent tools first: GA4, Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one proof point tied to recent work instead of more tools, e.g. “Built reporting infrastructure supporting enterprise web decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider merging or making one tools-only and the other outcomes/capabilities-focused.
- “Dashboarding” is vague and overlaps with Looker Studio/Power BI; “dashboard development” or “leadership reporting” is stronger.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and concrete, since leadership, governance, and weekly video work are already covered in newer entries.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve execution across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Tighten the second sentence around distinct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and other multimedia content, and helped establish repeatable publishing workflows.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, production cadence, or workflow improvements.
- Clarify supervision modestly: use “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” only if people management was meaningful.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” duplicates the stronger 2018–2022 bullet about expanding a weekly advocacy video update.
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with later governance/operations language; keep this entry more hands-on and foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and underplays impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/research support and the “first podcast” achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research coordination, program support, and digital communications content.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and more achievement-led: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Trim vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with specific outputs if possible (e.g., web features, interviews, briefing materials, audio content).
- If you can, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video/editorial operations here; later entries show that progression more credibly.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads as a generic software inventory and overlaps with stronger multimedia claims elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize production capability and tools most relevant to recent leadership roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production Tools**
- Rewrite as: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream/studio production workflows • Podcast recording, editing and production**
- Use parallel phrasing: keep all items as tools or capabilities, not a mix of software and vague functions.
- If true, add one higher-value capability instead of another tool, e.g. **Broadcast-quality video editing** or **Hybrid event production**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with Topline Skills (“Livestreaming • Studio operations • Hybrid and virtual event production”); consider keeping the capability in one place only.
- “Podcast production” is already supported by earlier NACo experience; keep it here only if you want this section to reflect hands-on tools, not repeat experience.
